issues.description: Field 'numberOfLecturers' has inconsistent types between the problem specification and the solution implementation. The UML in the problem statement (problem_statement.md lines 63-68) declares numberOfLecturers: int, but the solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) declares the backing field as 'private byte numberOfLecturers;' (line 9) and uses a byte parameter in the constructor (line 13) and in the setter (line 50). The solution's getter returns int (line 46), which further exposes the inconsistency. This mismatch leaves students unsure which type to implement and may cause signature/usage or narrowing/widening confusions when following the UML or tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type of numberOfLecturers consistent across artifacts. Recommended: change the solution to use int everywhere — update the field to 'private int numberOfLecturers;', change the constructor parameter and the setter parameter to int, and ensure the getter returns int. Alternatively, if a byte is intentionally desired, update the problem statement UML to document 'numberOfLecturers: byte' and explain that choice. Prefer keeping int in both the UML and solution to match the specification and avoid implicit narrowing issues.
